executiveSummary: GM1509 identity, Gelderland and Veiligheidsregio Noord- en Oost-Gelderland assignment, 2025 resident control and representative-point containment are coherent. CBS reports 39,499 residents, 26.4% aged 65 or older and 5,692 one-person households; 32 neighbourhood rows sum to 39,495 (-4, -0.010%), a negligible annual rounding/suppression difference. The bundle retains four districts, fourteen BAG places, 28 BRT settlements, Varsseveld and Terborg stations, 65 scheduled-transit stop areas and eight Dutch logical border links. One Terborg BAG label point falls just outside the independently generalized boundary, so code/full-geometry membership must prevail over label-point containment. All ten canonical presets run deterministically at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across eight services. Release is nevertheless correction-required. The persistent river preset applies 2.619256 normalized inundation stress, grows affected residents from 3,249 at T+24 to 4,451 at T+72 and accrues 1,375,040.376 person-hours without an Oude IJssel/Aa-strang German rainfall boundary, gauge/forecast, Stuw Voorst or other control/defence state, footprint, arrival or recession; the value is never 2.62 physical metres. Eight active single hazards reuse the same complete neighbourhood ordering. An official combustible-nature source probe also preserves that order. The graph omits German links and turns A18/N18 and N317 series sections into exact mobility/care/supply calculations without operational state. Public water, utility, industrial, care and facility registers are context only; absent matches are Unknown/NoData rather than zero or safe.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM1509 official 2025 identity, neighbourhood, place and settlement inputs
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated municipality/regional snapshots retrieved 31 August 2026; CC BY 4.0 CBS and Public Domain Mark 1.0 BAG terms
supports: Official inputs identify GM1509 as Oude IJsselstreek in Gelderland and Veiligheidsregio Noord- en Oost-Gelderland, with 39,499 residents, density 290/km², 26.4% aged 65 or older and 5,692 one-person households. The centre [6.410582996795649, 51.918300973094446] lies inside the 2025 boundary.

Thirty-two neighbourhood rows in four districts sum to 39,495 residents, four below the municipal control (-0.010%); households total 17,475 and rounded age-65-plus rows total 10,410. Deterministic allocation adds four without rewriting published rows.

Fourteen BAG places and 28 BRT settlements retain compact cores, eleven buurtschappen, two gehuchten and rural ribbons. Allocated 'Verspreide huizen' rows total 6,525 residents and must not be collapsed into a single centroid.

The Terborg BAG label point lies outside the independently generalized polygon. This is a geometry edition/generalization caveat, not proof that the official place is outside GM1509; joins must use stable identifiers and full geometry.

Cars-per-household is null in two rows, district-heating and public-charging in all 32. Null/suppressed remains Unknown/NoData, never zero. Annual residents do not establish incident-time visitors, workers, pupils, patients, travellers or responders.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Waterbeheerprogramma 2022–2027, cross-border Oude IJssel, Aa-strang and dated drought context
evidenceSources.edition: Current authority pages inspected 3 September 2026; WBP 2022–2027; Aa-strang project 2023–2024; drought report issued 9 July 2026; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The water board states that the Oude IJssel begins in Germany and that heavy German rainfall flows into its Dutch management area; transboundary water quantity/quality therefore requires coordination. This is mechanism context, not a selected event boundary.

Its Aa-strang project traces the watercourse from the German border through Stuw Voorst/de Stakenborg to the Oude IJssel at Ulft and describes works along the reach. A project/control asset is not a live gate setting, discharge, capacity or flood defence state.

The 2022–2027 programme covers groundwater, beken, sloten, small rivers, wastewater treatment, drought/water nuisance and safe dikes. The water-nuisance page says intense/long rain particularly affects lower and built areas and requires storage and maintained conveyance. These are planning responsibilities, not a local T+72 hydraulic model.

A dated 9 July 2026 report recorded rapidly falling groundwater/water levels after only 4 mm rain since 23 June, low Rhine/IJssel levels and Oude-IJssel navigation restriction via Doesburg. It was a regional timestamped status, not a 3 September municipal observation or arbitrary scenario forcing.
Current planning, historic/project state and dated observation remain distinct. Missing present measurements, valid time or control state stays Unknown and must not be carried through T+72.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2025–2028, Crisisplan 2025–2028 and cross-border response context
evidenceSources.edition: Risk-profile period 2025–2028; crisis plan adopted 12 December 2024; official scenario/doctrine evidence, not live incident/resource state; blanket reuse licence not stated
supports: The nature-fire annex records 603 hectares/6.03 km² of nature in Oude IJsselstreek and distinguishes fuel, terrain access, available extinguishing water, drought, wind, recreation presence, smoke and scarce specialist capacity. It is not a selected ignition, perimeter or resource commitment.

The current crisis plan defines alerting, command, information, public care, mobility, medical operations, emission control and recovery roles. A role or milestone does not prove site, route, people, crew, equipment, capacity or completion.

VNOG's public cross-border work and Magdalena high-water exercise stress continuous Dutch-German information exchange, crisis communication and liaison. The exercise says some dike rings are transboundary, but it is not a selected GM1509/Oude-IJssel case.

Public guidance for water, power, cyber, dangerous substances, fire and flooding promotes 72-hour self-reliance. Guidance does not measure household stock, warning receipt, shelter or distribution capability.

evidenceSources.title: E04 — Tourism/nature, water recreation and municipal industrial-area context
evidenceSources.edition: Current municipal pages inspected 3 September 2026; linked tourism policy 2020–2024 is historical; inspected pages state no machine API or blanket analytical reuse licence
supports: The municipality identifies Halse Rug, Vennebulten, Idink-/Nibbelinkbos, Engbergen and Anholtse Broek plus rowing/canoeing on Oude IJssel and Aa-strang. It lists hotels, B&Bs, campsites, holiday homes, group accommodation and events, proving plausible variable presence but not counts or occupancy.

Its industrial-area page describes Ulft De Rieze, historically and currently linked to metal employment, as connected via N317 to A18 and close to Germany. It describes Varsseveld De Hofskamp as about 100 hectares near A18/N18 and the rail/bus station, with a planned 25-hectare VIP extension.
Economic and tourism descriptions are planning/land-use context, not hazardous inventory, release, plume, shift attendance, freight state, road throughput or emergency resource availability.
Municipal nature-fire, water/groundwater reporting and safety pages are public information, not current incident measurements or a source/perimeter.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — A18/N18, N317/N318/N330/N335/N816, stations and current transport reference context
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-light 1 August 2026; ProRail and GTFS generated snapshots inspected 3 September 2026; provincial N317 page current at access; source-specific open-data terms
supports: Eight generated Dutch boundary edges comprise A18 toward Doetinchem, N18 toward Oost Gelre, N317 toward both Doetinchem and Aalten, N318, N330, N335 and N816. A18/N18 share physical road-18 and the two N317 links share road-317; consecutive series ceilings are non-additive.
The provincial N317 page documents safety/flow work and directs users to live works/diversion information. A project page is not an incident restriction feed or proof of route availability.

Varsseveld and Terborg ProRail stations and 65 GTFS stop areas provide static location/schedule context. They do not establish trains/buses running, accessible rolling stock, direction, capacity, evacuation use or connection acceptance.

The graph lists only five Dutch municipal neighbours and no German destination or border link, despite municipal evidence treating German access as material. NWB is monthly/CC0 1.0; ProRail CC0 and GTFS best-effort context cannot establish incident throughput.

evidenceSources.title: E06 — LIWO flood information and timestamped water, weather-warning and road screens
supports: LIWO 2025.1.6 supplies professional flood-information layers requiring expert water-manager interpretation. A selected case needs source/boundary, defence/control state, footprint, native depth/velocity units, arrival/persistence/recession, probability, CRS, licence and NoData.
No Waterinfo observation or forecast point is contained in GM1509. RWS network absence cannot establish Oude IJssel/Aa-strang level, discharge, German rainfall, local control or groundwater state.

The KNMI 48-hour warning retrieval contains no warning record and the NDW current-situation snapshot assigns no valid geometry inside GM1509. Issue-time no-match neither validates exercise forcing nor proves roads open.

KNMI sources are CC BY 4.0 and Waterinfo/NDW CC0 unless component terms state otherwise. Every record requires issue/observation/valid/retrieval time, spatial support, revision/fault state and explicit affectsSimulation.

evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public hazardous-activity and combustible-nature WFS screens
evidenceSources.edition: Live public WFS retrieval 3 September 2026; individual REV records carry validity/registration times; nature metadata public-domain terms, local records valid since 2006
supports: A representative-geometry screen within the generalized GM1509 boundary returns 58 activity geometries/55 unique identifiers: 36 gas-tank, six wind, five residual, four refuelling, two gas/mining, one manure-digestion and one Seveso record, Kramp Nederland B.V. in Varsseveld.

The screen is an audit aid, not a legal spatial determination. Multiple geometries/categories may belong to one activity; REV exposes context and per-record time but no fixed public refresh cadence or explicit reuse-licence version was established.
Register presence is not live inventory, operation, release, fire/explosion/toxic plume, probability, exposed shift, shutdown or emergency zone. Zero matches in any class would not prove absence.

The IPO combustible-nature WFS returns three GM1509 source polygons, all mixed forest, with generic names and validity beginning 24 May 2006. Public Domain source eligibility is not current fuel moisture, ignition, perimeter, smoke, access, occupancy or suppression.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / KVK-PDOK / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E08 — Partial water-chain, utility, telecom, facility and external-care context
evidenceSources.edition: HWH snapshot retrieved 3 September 2026, CC BY-SA 4.0; other public-context snapshots retrieved 31 August–3 September 2026 with source-specific editions/licences
supports: Full-resolution containment assigns 126 HWH points: twelve sewer pumps, two wastewater-treatment plants, 109 weirs, two surface-water pumps and one sluice. The contributor-dependent registry lacks complete catchment/pipe topology, comparable capacity, settings, power/control/backup, maintenance and live state.

The Public Domain provider query at the municipal centre returns Liander electricity/gas, Vitens drinking water and Ziggo media, but no drainage provider. One point is not complete territory/topology; empty drainage is Unknown, not absence of municipal/water-board duty.

One postcode sample maps to Liander OS ULFT 10-1i and reports 69/38 MW existing/required withdrawal, a 5.7 MW/28-request queue, 69/40 MW injection, and 27 projects with earliest year 2030. This is large-user planning, not current load, outage, reserve, switching or restoration.

Municipal screens contain 82 RDI antenna installations, 27 DUO education locations and seven KVK-PDOK government addresses. Registers do not prove coverage/backhaul/power, people, shelter function, accessibility, stock or operation.

RIVM assigns no emergency department inside GM1509. Slingeland Ziekenhuis in Doetinchem lies about 10.74 km straight-line from the representative centre and reports 24/7 emergency/acute-obstetric care, twelve rooms and 17,000 visits in 2025; annual CC0 context does not establish road time, ambulance, acceptance, staffing, occupancy or backup.

identity.summary: GM1509, Oude IJsselstreek, Gelderland and Veiligheidsregio Noord- en Oost-Gelderland are internally and officially coherent.
notes: Generated identity and exactly one safety-region assignment agree; the representative centre is contained by the 2025 geometry.
Terborg's generalized-boundary label-point mismatch is retained as an edition/generalization caveat, not a membership failure.
Annual/statistical, static planning/register, timestamped status, official scenario and synthetic output evidence remain distinct.

geography.summary: Administrative geography is mostly coherent, but transboundary water, local controls, pluvial/groundwater, fire and industrial source domains do not govern impacts.
notes: Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire reproduce the same complete 32-neighbourhood T+24 severity order.
River output selects no German boundary condition, Oude IJssel/Aa-strang reach, Stuw Voorst/other control, gauge, defence or inundation surface.
Pluvial output selects no AHN/soil/groundwater, catchment, sewer/storage/outfall or antecedent state.
Three official combustible-nature polygons and 55 unique REV activities remain non-causal context; full source geometry should govern eligible incidents.

demography.summary: Official resident control and neighbourhood totals reconcile within negligible CBS rounding/suppression difference.
notes: CBS reports 39,499 residents; 32 rows sum to 39,495 (-4, -0.010%) and deterministic allocation reconciles exactly.
The 26.4% age-65-plus share and 5,692 one-person households inform aggregate assistance pressure but do not identify individuals or preparedness.
Residents remain separate from accommodation guests, recreation/event visitors, pupils, patients, industrial/agricultural workers, travellers and responders under CORR-015.

regionalDetail.summary: Thirty-two neighbourhoods support census allocation, while null statistics and live water, utility, industrial and care state remain incomplete.
notes: Most CBS fields cover 30–32 rows; district heating and public charging cover none. Missing is Unknown/NoData.
One generalized label-point exception needs code/full-polygon joins and must not drop Terborg or create an outside population.
Registers, provider territory, planning capacity and facility addresses have incompatible coverage, cadence, licence and operational meaning.

settlements.summary: Fourteen BAG places and 28 BRT settlements preserve the dispersed core/buurtschap/gehucht structure.
notes: Settlement labels include Breedenbroek, Etten, Gendringen, Megchelen, Netterden, Silvolde, Sinderen, Terborg, Ulft, Varsseveld and smaller rural places.
Fourteen dispersed-house neighbourhoods contain 6,525 allocated residents; routing, warning and welfare cannot assume one central access point.
Labels and residents do not establish day/night presence, road state, fire eligibility, flood protection or service continuity.

transport.summary: Dutch boundary links, two stations and timetables omit German connectivity and do not form an incident-valid access/care/supply graph.
notes: A18/N18 and the two N317 links are series sections on shared physical corridors; eight logical edges are not eight independent evacuation capacities.
No German edge/destination is represented although the municipal economy and water system explicitly rely on cross-border context.
Varsseveld/Terborg stations and 65 GTFS stop areas are static; no train/bus operation, accessibility, capacity or emergency use is bound.
Slingeland acute care is external, and zero NDW matches cannot prove N317/A18/local/rural routes open.

emergencyContext.summary: Official water, fire, industrial, warning, mobility, care and 72-hour doctrine is not selected into incident/action/resource state.
notes: No selected river/rain/fire/industrial/cyber source, water-control state, route restriction, visitor/worker estimate, hospital acceptance or operator condition drives outputs.
Plans, registers and official scenario/doctrine establish responsibilities and plausible mechanisms, not activation, resources or completion.
Dated July drought context cannot be treated as current September state or projected to T+72.
Empty local operational matches are coverage facts, never zero hazard, open routes or available services.

scenarioMatrix.summary: All ten canonical presets execute at all six checkpoints for all eight services.
notes: The initial MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1509 pnpm audit:model gate passed one file/two tests in 31.05 seconds; structural success does not establish calibration.

Maximum severity / maximum affected / T+72 attributable person-hours are storm 0.474215 / 0 / 315,922.770; pluvial 0.365805 / 0 / 260,914.902; river 0.817269 / 4,451 / 1,375,040.376; coastal 0.057887 / 0 / 166,715.614; heat 0.451132 / 0 / 146,927.746.
Decimals are deterministic exercise outputs, not observations, forecasts, casualties, evacuees, measured outages or operator commitments.

numericalInvariants.summary: Outputs satisfy finite, deterministic, zero-intensity, layer-invariance, local reconciliation and causal-ledger contracts.
notes: Required structure/range, local-sum, repeatability and event-attributable accounting checks pass.
Allocated neighbourhood populations sum exactly to 39,499 while published rows retain their four-person difference.
Every zero-intensity preset returns exact-zero event hazard, affected resident-equivalents and attributable deprivation.
The legacy floodDepthM field is normalized inundation stress under CORR-017, not metres; river 2.619256 must never be labelled physical depth.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Shared seeding overrides transboundary hydraulics, pluvial/groundwater, weather, heat, fire/smoke, cyber and industrial geography.
notes: Eight active single hazards all start Ulft-Noord, Verspreide huizen Etten, Verspreide huizen Gendringen, Verspreide huizen Sinderen, Breedenbroek, Milt en Wieken and Heelweg; all end with Verspreide huizen Varsseveld, Ulft-Centrum/Oost and Verspreide huizen Terborg/Heuven.
This complete order is incompatible with distinct watercourses/controls, built drainage, forest sources, industrial sites, transport/utility targets and heat exposure.

A controlled T+24 ignition at the representative point of official mixed-forest polygon OudeIJsselstreek152 gives fire 0.537412, smoke 0.514009 and 693 affected but preserves the same ranking, with no authoritative fuel, wind, presence or suppression binding.
Earthquake T+24 is exact zero but has residual person-hours from earlier forcing; no selected event/ground-motion surface supports local interpretation.

serviceDependencies.summary: Exact service availability exceeds verified road, water-chain, utility, telecom, industrial, care and supply topology/state evidence.
notes: At compound T+24 availability is Power 0.827228, Water 0.781956, Drainage 0.778587, Gas 0.900004, Telecom 0.696184, Mobility 0.904056, Facilities 0.713977 and Supply 0.787697.

Provider polygons, one grid sample, 126 water objects, 82 antennas, 27 schools, seven government addresses, 55 REV activities and route/facility registers do not form compatible live topology, capacity, backup or restoration evidence.
No drainage provider is returned at the reference point; this is Unknown coverage, not zero drainage duty or infrastructure.
Water controls and rural/industrial assets imply power/control/access dependencies, but exact loss cannot be inferred without connectivity and incident state.

causalTrace.summary: The numerical causal ledger closes, but selected causes, cross-border inputs, controls, owners, actions and resources are absent.
notes: Outputs expose hazard, direct-service, interdependency, network, recovery and local-allocation components with matched totals.
Person-hours are synthetic counterfactual accounting, not observed outage duration, deaths, displacement or unmet care.
No German rainfall/flow, gate/weir/defence action, fire/industrial source, road/rail intervention, utility switching or hospital acceptance explains the trajectories.
Every state change needs authority/owner, target, prerequisite, route, resource, start/end, state, evidence class/time and uncertainty.

recovery72h.summary: Persistent river/compound disruption and other exact recovery curves lack incident, action, resource and blocker evidence through T+72.
notes: River stress remains 2.619256 from T+24 through T+72, affected grows 3,249 to 4,451, Facilities falls 0.871658 to 0.717441 and seven service values freeze, without boundary hydrograph, control action, inundation propagation or resource state.
Compound stress remains 0.311862 and affected grows 3,563 to 3,903 while every service worsens slightly; no physical action or constraint supports 1,339,635.112 person-hours.
Storm/pluvial/wildfire forcing clears by T+72 while burden continues accumulating to 315,922.770/260,914.902/131,468.329 without verified clearance, inspection or repair actions.

T+0–6 needs source selection/warning and cross-border/water/route verification; T+6–24 needs control, evacuation, fire/industrial, care and utility actions; T+24–72 needs dewatering, repair, welfare/supply and restoration evidence.

findings.summary: Official 2025 identity, resident control and stable regional membership reconcile.
findings.evidence: E01 and audit:context verify GM1509/Oude IJsselstreek/Gelderland/VNOG, a contained reference point and a four-resident (-0.010%) rounding difference. The Terborg label-point/generalized-boundary exception is explicitly retained rather than used to reject official membership.
findings.action: Retain edition, full polygons, stable codes, exact nulls and deterministic reconciliation; never join by label point/name alone.

findings.summary: Persistent river inundation is unsupported without a selected German–Oude IJssel/Aa-strang boundary and control/defence case.
findings.evidence: River T+24/T+72 reports normalized stress 2.619256, severity 0.817269, affected 3,249→4,451 and burden 351,891.297→1,375,040.376. E02 establishes cross-border inflow, Aa-strang, Stuw Voorst and the Oude IJssel at Ulft, but no German rainfall/flow, gauge/forecast, gate/weir/defence state, footprint, arrival, recession or probability is selected. The stress is not metres.
findings.action: Suppress exact consequence until WRiJ/LIWO expert selection binds named watercourse/reach, upstream boundary, datum/unit, gauge/forecast, control/defence state, footprint, arrival/persistence/recession, issue/valid time, probability, uncertainty, licence and NoData.

findings.summary: Direct coastal zero does not validate inland water safety and still drives unexplained deprivation.
findings.evidence: GM1509 is inland; coastal T+24 has zero inundation stress/affected but wind 19.823888 m/s and 46,909.130 person-hours, growing to 166,715.614 at T+72. Direct North Sea non-applicability is not evidence about Oude IJssel, Aa-strang, local drainage or German inflow, and no incident-specific wind observation/forecast explains the service burden.
findings.action: Label direct North Sea flooding Not applicable only for that source scope; keep connected inland water Unknown unless selected separately. Require event-valid wind forcing for indirect coastal-preset effects or suppress local consequence.

findings.summary: Generic pluvial stress is disconnected from terrain, groundwater, catchments, sewers, storage, watercourses and controls.
findings.evidence: Pluvial T+24 reports rain zero, stress 0.301712, affected zero and Drainage 0.891759; storm T+24 retains stress 0.130317 after rain/wind zero. E02 distinguishes lower/built water nuisance, groundwater, storage and conveyance, while E08 identifies 126 partial assets. No AHN/soil surface, antecedent moisture/groundwater, sewer/catchment, outfall, receiving level, capacity, power or control state is bound.
findings.action: Integrate versioned municipal/WRiJ stress, AHN, soil/groundwater, catchment, sewer/storage/outfall and control inputs with event definition, CRS, units, licence and NoData. Asset registers remain contextual until topology/capacity/state are verified.

findings.summary: Eight unrelated active hazards reuse one exact complete neighbourhood ordering.
findings.evidence: Storm, pluvial, river, coastal, heat, winter, cyber and wildfire share all 32 T+24 ranks, from Ulft-Noord through the same top seven to the same bottom three. Cross-border water, urban drainage, industrial sites, roads, heat, mixed forests and cyber targets have distinct physical support. A controlled official-forest ignition leaves the order unchanged.
findings.action: Replace shared seeding with mechanism-specific hydraulic, groundwater/pluvial, wind, heat, source/perimeter/plume, industrial and cyber surfaces over full geometry. Add tests preventing unrelated hazards from silently sharing the complete rank.

findings.summary: Wildfire and smoke effects are not contained by an authoritative source, fuel or response state.
findings.evidence: VNOG records 603 ha of municipal nature and IPO returns three mixed-forest polygons. Default wildfire produces zero flame, smoke 0.342539, zero affected and Water 0.782012 at T+24. Placing ignition at official polygon OudeIJsselstreek152 produces fire 0.537412, smoke 0.514009 and 693 affected but preserves the generic order. Neither test has fuel moisture, event wind, perimeter, occupancy, access, extinguishing water or suppression.
findings.action: Require an eligible polygon/source/perimeter, event-valid fuel/weather/plume, timestamped exposed cohorts, access, water and suppression state. Missing source is Unknown/no selected event; a regional risk phase or old polygon never becomes a forecast.

findings.summary: Resident-only exposure omits rural, tourism, event, industrial, school, rail/road and care cohorts.
findings.evidence: Fourteen dispersed-house rows contain 6,525 allocated residents across 28 settlements; official pages identify campsites/group accommodation, nature/water recreation, events and major industrial areas. Two stations, 65 stops, 27 schools and businesses imply non-resident activity. The model uses only 39,499 residents and cannot represent seasonal/day-night people, workers or travellers.
findings.action: Keep CBS residents authoritative and add separate privacy-safe timestamped guest, visitor/event, pupil, worker, patient, traveller and responder ranges with source, validity, uncertainty and anti-double-counting under CORR-015. Missing presence remains Unknown.

findings.summary: A18/N18/N317 series corridors, rural/rail access, German links and external acute care are not operationally represented.
findings.evidence: A18/N18 and two N317 edges are non-additive series corridors, while the graph has no German neighbour/link. Stations/stops lack operation state and rural approaches/crossings are absent. Slingeland is 10.74 km straight-line outside GM1509, but no valid route, ambulance, acceptance/diversion, staffing, occupancy or backup is bound. Compound still emits Mobility 0.904056 and Supply 0.787697; zero NDW matches does not mean open.
findings.action: Build authority-reviewed Dutch/German multimodal corridors and internal approaches with physical identity, direction/mode, crossing/restriction, passability, emergency priority, valid time and unit throughput. Bind care/supply/mutual aid to route, vehicle and acceptance state; otherwise output Unknown.

findings.summary: Material industrial/external-safety context has no source-selectable hazard or response workflow.
findings.evidence: Municipal pages identify Ulft metal industry and Varsseveld Hofskamp/VIP beside strategic road/rail links. The scoped REV screen returns 55 unique activities, including one Seveso site, 36 gas tanks, four refuelling sites, two gas facilities and manure digestion. None of the ten presets selects an installation, substance/inventory, fire/explosion/toxic release, plume/runoff, shift presence or emergency zone; generic cyber/compound values are not substitutes.
findings.action: Offer an authority-selected industrial scenario adapter using versioned REV geometry only as source context, then require current operator/authority incident class, inventory/release bounds, weather/plume/runoff, exposed objects, protective actions and uncertainty. Never auto-trigger from register presence.

findings.summary: Partial water, provider, grid, telecom and facility context cannot calibrate exact eight-service availability.
findings.evidence: E08 exposes 126 partial water objects, Liander/Vitens/Ziggo responsibility, no drainage match, one grid-planning sample, 82 antennas, 27 schools, seven government addresses and external care. It lacks compatible topology, live load/pressure/quality/backhaul, damage, backup, priority users, stock, crews and restoration. Compound T+24 nevertheless emits eight exact availability decimals.
findings.action: Integrate authorized timestamped aggregate operations/topology where lawful and safe; otherwise expose explicitly synthetic versioned zones/ranges. Preserve contributor coverage, sensitive topology, nulls and no-matches as Unknown and suppress operator-looking precision.

findings.summary: Planning, dated status, registers, empty screens and six-decimal synthetic output need adjacent evidence/time/NoData semantics.
findings.evidence: The UI can combine annual CBS, WBP/project/control context, a 9 July drought report, risk-profile scenarios, historic nature polygons, live-register records, no local Waterinfo/KNMI/NDW point and exact outputs. These are not interchangeable. River 2.619256 is especially liable to be mistaken for metres, while empty warnings/roads can be mistaken for safe/open.
findings.action: Attach publisher, dataset/version, licence, evidence class, issue/observation/valid/retrieval/expiry, spatial coverage, uncertainty, NoData and affectsSimulation to every value/layer/export. Stale/non-overlapping inputs deactivate; normalized stress is never labelled depth/metres.

findings.summary: First-72-hour deterioration, persistence and recovery lack confirmed cross-border inputs, actions, resources and blockers.
findings.evidence: River forcing freezes while affected grows 3,249→4,451 and Facilities declines; compound affected grows 3,563→3,903 while all services worsen. Cleared storm/pluvial/fire forcing still accumulates large burden. No warning, German liaison/input, gate/weir/defence action, evacuation, road/rail restriction, fire/industrial response, hospital acceptance, utility switching, crew/material/fuel/water, shelter/welfare, restocking, dewatering or inspection explains the curves.
findings.action: Add T0/6/12/24/48/72 incident/action/resource/blocker records with authority/owner, cross-border status, target, request/confirmation/dispatch/active/completion, route, capacity, dependency, valid/expiry time and uncertainty. Unsupported change remains synthetic/Unknown and non-decision-grade.

corrections.summary: Replace generic GM1509 water outputs with selected cross-border Oude IJssel/Aa-strang, control/defence, pluvial and groundwater mechanisms.
corrections.validation: Every river/pluvial consequence has named reach/source, German boundary, datum/unit, gauge/forecast, initial/control/defence state, footprint, issue/valid time, uncertainty and NoData; direct North Sea non-applicability never means inland-water safe and stress is never metres.

corrections.summary: Replace shared spatial seeding, enforce source-contained fire and separate residents from dynamic rural/activity cohorts.
corrections.validation: Eight hazard families do not share all 32 ranks; official eligible forest ignition prioritizes source/adjacent geometry with fuel, plume, access/water/suppression evidence. Residents and time-varying guests/workers/travellers remain separate, reconciled cohorts.

corrections.summary: Represent A18/N18/N317 common-mode sections, internal/rural/rail and German-border routes plus external care as valid-time workflows.
corrections.validation: Series edges never add capacity; Dutch/German destinations, internal approaches, crossings, rail/bus and restrictions carry mode/direction/passability/validity/throughput. Slingeland/alternatives require ambulance route and acceptance state; empty NDW does not mean open.

corrections.summary: Add source-selectable industrial/external-safety scenarios without promoting REV presence to an incident.
corrections.validation: REV retains record ID, geometry/category, validity, coverage, licence uncertainty and affectsSimulation=false. Only an authority-selected activity with release bounds, weather/plume/runoff, exposure and protective actions becomes causal; no record or no incident remains Unknown/no selected event.

corrections.summary: Govern partial lifeline context and make T0–T+72 service/recovery changes depend on confirmed operations.

residualLimitations: No selected WRiJ/LIWO case establishes a GM1509 German rainfall/flow boundary, Oude IJssel/Aa-strang gauge/forecast, Stuw Voorst or other control/defence state, footprint, depth/velocity, arrival or recession. Generic precision is not evidence.
No contained Waterinfo point covers the local water system. RWS point absence and a dated WRiJ regional drought article cannot be spatialized, treated as current or projected through T+72.

The 126 HWH objects identify possible controls/water-chain assets but not complete catchments, hydraulic/sewer connectivity, comparable capacity, settings, power/control/backup, maintenance or live state.
Municipal/WRiJ pluvial and groundwater products require native version, CRS, event/antecedent conditions, units, licence and explicit NoData before analytical use.

Complete electricity, gas, drinking-water, drainage, telecom, care and supply topology, live load/outage, backup, crews, spares, fuel and restoration are unavailable or security-sensitive; public territories/registers cannot replace them.

Eight Dutch logical edges omit Germany and overstate independence where A18/N18 or N317 sections are series. NWB, stations, 65 GTFS stops and zero NDW situations do not establish event-time operation, passability, emergency priority or throughput.
RIVM/Slingeland data do not expose ambulance availability, staffing, dispatch, acceptance/diversion, occupancy, backup or restoration; protected operational information must not be inferred.

CBS residents omit guests, recreation/event visitors, pupils, patients, industrial/agricultural workers, rail/road travellers and responders. No inspected public feed supplies privacy-safe incident-time presence.
Three historic-validity mixed-forest polygons and 603 ha regional-profile nature coverage do not supply current fuel/moisture, ignition, perimeter, plume, access, extinguishing water or suppression.

The REV screen is representative-geometry audit context, not a legal spatial determination or live operation/inventory. Its fixed public cadence/licence version remains unresolved and records never imply a release.
One Liander planning sample is not municipal coverage or outage state; empty drainage provider matching is incomplete/Unknown, not zero infrastructure.
Antenna, education and government registers have different scope/cadence/licence and remain affectsSimulation=false without reviewed causal bindings.
No assigned warning, fixed weather, water, road, local acute-care, PM2.5 or seismic point is a coverage/time fact, not zero hazard, disruption, pollution, need or service continuity.
The Terborg BAG label-point mismatch is a generalized-geometry caveat; label points cannot decide official place membership or analytical containment.

Exact hazard, affected, service, recovery and person-hour outputs remain synthetic exercises, not forecasts or decision-grade advice until critical/high findings are corrected and relevant Dutch/German authorities review the case.
This audit covers only 72 hours; flood recession, contamination, displacement, industrial recovery and infrastructure repair can last substantially longer.
